[SQL: INSERT INTO paper (title, year, method, publish, category, code_id, abstract, evaluation) VALUES
(
    'FirmAgent: Leveraging Fuzzing to Assist LLM Agents with IoT Firmware Vulnerability Discovery',
    2026,
    'Hybrid Fuzzing + LLM Agent with Taint Propagation and PoC Generation. Uses fuzzing to accurately identify input-related source points, then employs an LLM agent for context-aware taint propagation analysis from source to sink, and another LLM agent for automatic proof-of-concept generation. A lightweight pre-fuzzing analysis extracts service handlers, keyword dictionaries, and sink distance maps.',
    'NDSS 2026',
    'Hybrid Fuzzing + LLM Static Analysis',
    15,
    'FirmAgent is the first hybrid solution that leverages fuzzing to assist LLM agents in finding vulnerabilities in IoT firmware. It addresses the key limitations of both static analysis (high false positives, no PoC) and dynamic fuzzing (high false negatives). Fuzzing accurately identifies taint source points, then an LLM agent performs context-aware taint propagation analysis, and another generates PoC testcases. Tested on 14 real-world IoT router firmware, it found 182 vulnerabilities with 91%% precision, including 140 0-day vulnerabilities and 17 CVEs.',
    'Evaluated on 14 real-world IoT router firmware. Achieved 91%% precision (182/200 confirmed), compared to EmTaint (37%%), HermeScan (33%%), Greenhouse (40%%). Discovered 140 previously unknown vulnerabilities, 17 with CVE IDs. Ablation study showed removing fuzzing information drops precision from 91%% to 74%%. PoC auto-generation success rate: 91.8%%.'
),
(
    'IoTBec: An Accurate and Efficient Recurring Vulnerability Detection Framework for Black Box IoT Devices',
    2026,
    'Vulnerability Interface Signature (VIS) + LLM-Driven Fuzzing. Constructs a firmware-independent Vulnerability Interface Signature (VIS) from black-box interface analysis and known CVE information. Matches VIS against target devices, then uses an LLM fuzzing agent to generate highly targeted mutation payloads for validation. Operates without firmware or source code access.',
    'NDSS 2026',
    'Black-Box LLM-Driven Fuzzing',
    16,
    'IoTBec is a novel firmware and source-code independent framework for recurring vulnerability detection in black-box IoT devices. It constructs a Vulnerability Interface Signature (VIS) from black-box interfaces and known vulnerability information, then integrates signature-based matching with LLM-driven fuzzing for automated validation. On devices from 5 major IoT vendors, IoTBec discovered 7x more vulnerabilities than SOTA black-box fuzzers, achieving 100%% precision and 93.37%% recall. Overall 183 vulnerabilities detected, 169 assigned CVE IDs, including 53 new ones (avg CVSS 8.61).',
    'Tested on devices from 5 major IoT vendors. Discovered avg 7x more vulnerabilities than SOTA black-box fuzzers. 100%% alert precision, 93.37%% recall. 183 total vulnerabilities, 169 CVE IDs. 53 newly discovered (avg CVSS 8.61). LLM fuzzing discovered 25 vulnerabilities beyond ground truth (4 completely novel). Covers buffer overflow, command injection, and CSRF.'
),
(
    'Energy-Efficient Multi-LLM Reasoning for Binary-Free Zero-Day Detection in IoT Firmware',
    2025,
    'Tri-LLM Architecture (LLaMA + DeepSeek + GPT-4o) + Energy-Aware Symbolic Load Model. A binary-free, architecture-agnostic solution using three LLMs: LLaMA-based configuration interpreter, DeepSeek-based structural abstraction analyzer, and GPT-4o semantic fusion model. Introduces LLM computational signatures (latency patterns, uncertainty markers, reasoning depth) and formal mathematical foundations for monotonicity, divergence, and energy-risk coupling.',
    'arXiv preprint (arXiv:2512.19945)',
    'Binary-Free Zero-Day Detection',
    17,
    'This paper proposes a binary-free, architecture-agnostic solution for zero-day vulnerability detection in IoT firmware, addressing scenarios where firmware is encrypted, stripped, or inaccessible. Unlike methods requiring binary visibility or emulation, it uses only high-level descriptors and a tri-LLM reasoning architecture combining LLaMA, DeepSeek, and GPT-4o. It formally derives mathematical foundations (monotonicity, divergence, energy-risk coupling) and incorporates computational signatures and energy-aware modeling. Simulation shows high exposure conditions increase zero-day likelihood by 20-35%% across models, with GPT-4o showing strongest cross-layer correlations.',
    'Simulation-based evaluation across multi-LLM pipeline. High exposure conditions increased predicted zero-day likelihood by 20-35%%. GPT-4o demonstrated strongest cross-layer correlations and highest sensitivity. Energy and divergence metrics significantly predicted elevated risk. Formal mathematical proofs establish monotonicity, divergence, and energy-risk coupling properties. Novel contribution: works without any binary/code/firmware access.'
);]
